document_title: Asked inside the chart. UTMB's OpenEvidence account beside Texas law
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
A Texas statute and a UTMB release both describe AI in the health record.

UTMB in Galveston put OpenEvidence inside its health record in March. Clinicians get answers with citations. More than half of them use it for "clinical decision support," UTMB said on September 22nd.

Since September 1st, 2025, Sec. 183.005 of the Health and Safety Code has said a practitioner who uses AI for "diagnostic purposes" must disclose that use to patients. The record here can't say whether the section reaches this use.

A patient can ask in the exam room. The UT System Regents meet November 18th to 19th in Austin. The public may testify on a topic the agenda lists. A speaker sends the board's General Counsel a name and topic at least 24 hours ahead.

Will the November agenda list AI in the health record?

#UTMB #Galveston #UTSystem

S1.headline: The question is asked inside the chart
S1.body: UTMB says the AI platform OpenEvidence puts cited medical evidence inside the UTMB electronic health record. It announced the collaboration on September 22nd. The cart and the lights are drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: An answer with its sources
S2.body: Clinicians sign in with their UTMB credentials and ask in plain language. Answers cite medical literature and guidelines, UTMB says. The tool went live in March.
strings: Clinicians sign in with their UTMB credentials and ask in plain language. Answers cite medical literature and guidelines, UTMB says. The tool went live in March.

S3.headline: Four hospital campuses
S3.body: UTMB has hospitals on four campuses and more than 100 clinics across Southeast Texas. One cart is drawn for each campus, to illustrate.
strings: UTMB has hospitals on four campuses and more than 100 clinics across Southeast Texas. One cart is drawn for each campus, to illustrate.

S4.headline: More than half of its clinicians use it
S4.body: That is UTMB's own figure. The release prints no count of clinicians and no total. The fill stops at half and is left open past it.
strings: More than half of its clinicians use it

S5.headline: Use is reported. No test is printed.
S5.body: UTMB's release prints no accuracy, error or outcome figure. UTMB says it will keep evaluating use. The bars are a different tool, an MRI model of survival in brain metastases with UTMB radiology authors, scored by C-index.

S6.headline: UTMB's other AI platform
S6.body: UTMB's Qualified Health agreement began at $825,000. Item 65 on the Regents' August consent agenda would take it to $9,850,000 across all seven UT health institutions. It never names OpenEvidence, so the cart's screen is dark.
strings: UTMB's Qualified Health agreement began at $825,000. Item 65 on the Regents' August consent agenda would take it to $9,850,000 across all seven UT health institutions. It never names OpenEvidence, so the cart's screen is dark.

S7.headline: The law has a disclosure line
S7.body: Since September 1st, 2025, Sec. 183.005 says a practitioner who uses AI for "diagnostic purposes" must disclose it to patients. UTMB calls its use "clinical decision support." The record here can't say whether the section reaches this use.

S8.body: Which tool was used? Did it shape the plan? Texas law has practitioners disclose AI used for diagnostic purposes.
